nodes.title: Color & Memory: Works by Elena Vasquez

body.processed:
"Color & Memory" presents 35 paintings by Elena Vasquez, spanning two decades of her career exploring the intersections of personal memory, cultural heritage, and chromatic expression.

About the Exhibition

Vasquez's large-scale canvases use vivid color fields to evoke the emotional landscapes of memory. Drawing on her Mexican-American heritage, the works reference family gatherings, childhood landscapes, and the passage of time through shifting palettes that range from sun-drenched yellows and oranges to contemplative blues and violets.

Gallery Guide

  • Gallery 1: Early Works (2006-2012) - Foundations of memory
  • Gallery 2: The Migration Series (2013-2018) - Displacement and belonging
  • Gallery 3: Recent Works (2019-2026) - Synthesis and reflection

Free audio guide available for download on our mobile app.

nodes.title: New Perspectives: Emerging Artists of the Pacific Northwest

body.processed:
"New Perspectives" showcases the work of 12 emerging artists from the Pacific Northwest, selected from over 400 applicants to our annual juried exhibition.

Featured Artists

This year's exhibition features works in painting, sculpture, photography, mixed media, and digital art that challenge conventional boundaries and offer fresh interpretations of contemporary themes.

Themes

  • Environmental resilience and the changing landscape
  • Digital identity in the age of AI
  • Community and belonging in urban spaces
  • The intersection of craft and fine art traditions

The exhibition is accompanied by a catalog with essays by art critic Michael Torres and interviews with each artist.

The Meridian Sculpture Garden features 24 large-scale outdoor sculptures set among native plantings and walking paths on the grounds of the Meridian Arts Center.

Collection Highlights

  • "Convergence" by Richard Serra - Two curving steel plates creating a contemplative passageway
  • "Wind Harps" by Liz Larner - Sound-producing kinetic sculpture that responds to wind
  • "Ancestor Stones" by Isamu Noguchi - Three carved granite forms honoring the land
  • "Digital Bloom" by TeamLab - Interactive light installation (evening viewing)

Visiting the Garden

The Sculpture Garden is open daily from dawn to dusk, with free admission. Guided tours are available Saturdays and Sundays at 11:00 AM and 2:00 PM. Self-guided tour brochures are available at the Visitor Center.
